english: A tense scene.
Oh, a cleric! Just in time.
Four young guys, each looking a bit nervous.
Four young guys, just hanging around, looking normal.
Except the angry-looking blonde kid.
We've confiscated the illegal goods, he says and bows his head.
For the city!
He turns his head towards one of the kids behind him.
How's it going, Urth-Nisse?
I'm trying. Hold on.
Are you militia?
Great job, kid.
(Point at the lanky kid trying to cast a cantrip.) "Hey. Stop it."
The blond kid shakes his head.
He smiles. "Thank you, Cleric!"
He freezes and gives the blonde kid a nervous look.
Oh. Sorry, Cleric.
You see Rollo waving towards him. A gesture for him to ignore your comment.
I'm Rollo, the blonde kid says and takes a bow. "Rollo Malach! At your service. Behind me are Urth-Nisse, Stenbusken, and Toli. We're members of the Norvikian Resistance, a movement to-"
You're thieves!
And ignorant book burners!
The girl adjusts her spectacles and straightens her back.
With all due respect, Mr. Cleric, she says. "Don't believe a word from these thugs."
You notice the two other girls behind her, a halfling and a dwarf, both look at each other.
Assholes!
Careful, it's an actual cleric...
Thugs? Come on, Modissa. Really? Like the AY aren't just a bunch of ruffians!
I've seen enough, the goblin whispers to you and sighs. "Just activists clashing."
Hello everyone! I'm The Cleric.
I'm confused. Is there a problem here?
(Just let them continue arguing.)
Azgalist Youths.
See her green armband?
Problem's taken care of, Lord Cleric.
Oh- fuck off.
They've stolen, she hisses, then turns to Rollo to bark out, "You STOLE, our entire Waterlane delivery!"
Yeah, sure. Of an illegal newspaper.
Lord Cleric, I assure you, we're doing the city a favor here.
I take that back. It's just a bunch of larpers.
I see. It's a lover's quarrel.
Lord Cleric? Hm. I dig it. I'm The Lord Cleric.
Wait a second. No... I need to correct something here. I'm not actually a cleric.
Okay. So, I'm sensing a conflict here.
Are you kids even allowed to be out this late?
What?! No!
He's blushing.
The girl gives you an incredulous frown.
And she's disgusted.
That's not- Cleric. Focus.
Oh. Sure!
You're not?
The guy behind him starts to stutter out, "W-what are you then? Like... what?"
I am actually a bad-ass rogue.
Can't you see I'm a powerful wizard?
A what?
You know. The swashbuckling kind.
You know. A thief.
You know. Sneaky scout, or whatever.
...Ridiculous. She mutters to herself and presses her face into her hands.
She's sooo over it.
A better rogue would have gotten a better reaction, methinks.
Ah! Like a cleric-wizard!
Sure. I'll take it.
<shake>No!</shake> Why can't you get this through your thick skulls?! (Stamp your feet.)
Just a wizard, please.
They're taken aback by your exclamation.
What's wrong with this guy? the halfling says to the dwarf girl.
Okay. We can... we can do that.
As you shuffle your feet around, all the teenagers look at you in disapproval.
...Okay.
A... druid?
So we shouldn't call you a cleric, then?
Hm. No, for legal reasons you can keep calling me cleric.
I don't trust you to address me properly, so Lord Master Cleric is fine. Or something akin.
(Just stare at him, and breathe loudly.)
The blonde kid just nods slowly.
He does not understand you.
Both sides look at you with frowns.
Look, I have a hard time seeing how old humans are as well, but...
These are clearly young adults. Even if they're not acting their age.
Hey! Shut up, goblin!
Your companion grits his sharp fangs in the blonde kid's direction.
Hey, kid. Wanna die? Keep talking.
He takes a step back.
Impressive. The goblin stands his ground.
This goblin's got bite! Damn!
You're here to uphold the law, right?
So arrest these assholes!
Now!
The dwarf grabs her hand and holds her back. "Modissa... calm down. Please..."
(Point at the Azgal girl.) "You. Explain your side."
(Point at the Nationalist boy.) "Okay, you. What's going on here?"
What does the law say about this conflict?
What are you guys voting in the election?
M-"Okay. I've come to a conclusion."
She scoffs.
Okay. Fine.
Her dwarven friend mutters, "Modissa..." in a concerned tone.
Her friends are trying to keep her from being too brazen. Why? If they're in the right, she should be brazen.
We deliver papers for the Azgalian Chant. Maybe you've heard of it. It's a pretty big deal.
He chuckles.
The paper is not terribly popular. But it is known for radical articles and political stances.
She draws a sharp breath. "We have a busy schedule, and right as we started delivering the papers in Waterlane, these pieces of shit start following us."
Taking papers we've just delivered right out of people's mailboxes!
That's illegal, right? asks the halfling girl.
Highly illegal.
Somewhat illegal.
Just a bit illegal. Maybe.
Of course it's illegal!
Your opinion does not even register - she does not even hear it. Insolent behavior.
She does not care for your opinion on the legality of mail theft. How rude.
And then they grab one of our paper stacks from Xerba. Like, straight-up assault and theft and...!
Modissa, it wasn't...
They can't get away with this!
It probably was not that bad.
Poor girl.
First of all, thank you for listening to reason.
I know we look like some dumb kids, but we're not.
Something about his expression makes you think the exact opposite.
Burning the written word does nothing to dispel such a notion.
Yeah. No, these are dumb kids. No doubt.
He gestures towards you and then to himself. "We're on the same team here."
I don't look dumb.
He says, looking dumb.
Stop stalling. Tell me what you're doing here.
Uh-huh.
(Give him a hug.)
The boy physically clenches his entire posture up into a defensive wall as you move forward to embrace him - in a manly hug.
...Huh?
(Whisper.) "We're in this together, brother."
You're a good kid. Keep fighting the good fight.
(Release the hug.)
The blonde kid backs away from you with a bewildered look on his face.
The lack of a proper father figure will leave young boys unable to appreciate a manly hug.
He does not get hugged often.
Oh boy. They're going at it.
The halfling lets out a cheer.
Kiss! Kiss!
Modissa scoffs. "Right out of Skyline Boys."
Ugh.
Somehow, their comments taint this manly display of love.
That makes you feel bad.
So...
We heard about the Azgal Chant being delivered on Tolstad.
Or I did. At the Guild.
I work at the Fishery. And I see every day how Urthfolk get radicalized by dwarven nonsense.
So... I figured I'd get the boys with me and we'd... you know.
Put a stop to it.
You want to stop the production of a copper paper?
Through violence and terror?
(Glance at the pile of paper behind him.)
We, uh... couldn't figure out where the thing was printed or anything.
A lot of copper press zines don't really have official companies behind them.
Especially trash like the Chant, you hear coming from the short kid in the back.
Go fuck yourself Toli!
Hey, hey, relax! I'm telling our story here! To the good Lord Cleric!
He turns back to you and coughs once.
Of course, it's illegal to distribute unlicensed papers in every official district. So I ask around. Apparently, someone saw these girls at the University going around, delivering it.
Wasn't that difficult to figure out: it was Modissa doing the deliveries.
Fucking Modissa.
She's not allowed to do that, the large kid in the back says with a nod.
Wait, you guys know each other? There's history here?
(Turn to the girls.) "They don't like you, do they?"
Uh. Yeah.
They don't like women in general, she says with a frown.
Back in school everybody knew who Modissa was.
The 'Azgalist Annoyance', the blonde kid says with a grin.
Such a terrible nickname. Unimaginative and boring. Also fuck you.
Anyway, that's how we got here. They're delivering an illegal magazine, and we've put a stop to it.
He grins wide and proud.
The Azgal Chant - or whatever silly name its anonymous publisher gave it - is not licensed for distribution in Tolstad.
Requiring licenses for public distribution is a typical method to repress journalistic intent in Norvik.
The city knows that terrible papers should not be given out.
At the same time, it is also illegal to steal delivered newspapers from mailboxes.
Even if those papers are delivered illegally.
That's a lot of illegality.
Both are in the wrong?
In different ways, yes.
Although it's clear that the boys are bullies, and the girls are victims.
Your sense of justice says only one thing.
The newspapers are filled with ill-making propaganda.
Let it burn.
Not the time, Snell says, rubbing his eyes.
The Workers' Party, she says. "Duh."
Same for me!
The dwarf raises her hand, carefully. "Y-yeah."
And these stupid boys are obviously voting for the Party of Norvik.
No we're not. None of us are.
Yeah. Fuck that.
What?
Uh. Yeah. No.
The silent kid in the back raises his fist into the air. "Fuck the establishment."
Rollo nods to the Cleric. "There are deeper forces at work here."
Divine forces.
You should support the city, kid.
I see. You're also voting Azgalist, then? Same.
Oh. You're Freestriders? Very cool.
You should obviously vote for me.
Agrarian is... a good choice.
What, you're not voting for anything?
Oh, we are. But...
What? No!
What? Of course not. Fuck the Freestriders the most of all.
What? Are you on the ballot?
No. Just write THE CLERIC on your voting card, and that should be it.
One day... (Clench your fist.)
Uh. Okay. But... no.
Are they still around?
You shut your mouth! (Seethe.)
...No. They're not. (Seethe harder.)
He holds up his hands. "Hey, I have nothing against their original policies. But they all turned Azgal! So... no."
Indeed!
We're not voting. At all.
He looks insanely proud.
Not a bad choice, considering this mess.
You're apolitical? That's impressive. I am also apolitical. I don't engage with politics.
What? If you don't engage in democracy, the bad guys win!
Fair.
Apolitical?
That's not a thing.
It's a thing.
What? Really?
My aunt's apolitical. She says it's too much to think about with democracy. She liked it when Urth ruled.
My dad says the same, but he'll be voting for the Nationalists.
Oh. That's what my aunt does too. Maybe she's not apolitical...
Guys. Focus.
We, the blonde kid says, gesturing to his three friends.
We are fighting the evil powers- ready to establish a true resistance to anti-human sentiments.
For Urth!
The girl with the creased brow sighs loudly.
Urth be Blessed!
Interesting sentiment.
That sounds like a conspiracy...!
Take my god out of your mouth, kid.
He is!
Uh. Yeah!
Uh-huh. The blonde kid looks to his left and right. "Right on."
Uh- I'm-
He stutters and looks to the guys behind him.
Sorry.
With your witty sense of humor?
No. The spell.
That would be a solution.
Tell them you've made up your mind, and then cast it on one of them.
Tell them you're done here, and just cast it on them after that, or something.
Good, she says, and nods.
She's hiding a nervous expression.
Great! Uh... Good.
He's outwardly very nervous.
(Approach the blonde kid to see if you can get these Nationalists to back off.)
(Approach the girl with the spectacles to check if you can argue against these Azgals.)
Oh. Hey. He stares at you, trying to retain his composure.
He's terrified.
This can get out of hand quickly.
If you fail at telling him to give back the papers, this might get ugly.
Your body might grow irate.
You're frustrated already.
You're likely to take it out on both sides if you fail at getting them to give back the papers.
Beware.
(Stare at him.)
(Wave your fingers in front of his face.)
Are you good?
Tell him to give back the papers in a controlled and thoughtful manner.
(Step back.)
Uh...
His pores are sweating.
The kid is horrified by your helmed presence.
He flinches.
He looks away, and then to you.
I'm good.
For what? the large boy asks.
No, just good. Like a good person.
Oh. Makes sense.
You see the blonde kid take a deep breath.
What are you- hey.
She frowns as you approach.
What do you want?
They seem very defensive.
They are preparing for hostility.
So you're like an Azgalian gang leader, huh?
(Lean in close.) "You're not evil, are you?"
Construct an argument that makes her go away.
She tries to meet your question with a frown.
But she mostly just looks stressed out.
No. I'm just an Azgal, hard at work.
Mr. Cleric.
She glares at you.
No. Mr. Cleric.
Oh.
Regretfully, you should be informed.
There is no clear legal argument here to you.
What, really?
The very nature of this conflict lies in the fact that both sides have legal issues.
Whatever arguments you can come up with, she will refute them with the other side's illegality.
It's a 'what about' type situation.
So what do I do?
You find another way. Or... perhaps you simply rethink your strategy.
She squints at you for a few seconds before answering.
I do not require a license as a paper deliverer. My boss, the ACP - Azgalian Copper Printer - is fully in their right to print this paper.
Sâ de sâ.
Dwarven slang-phrase that means roughly, 'That's how it is.'
Her statement is true. But it dances around the fact that her boss is the one without the license to distribute in Tolstad.
You catch her eye twitching. Heh. She's nervous!
Perhaps. But you must engage in a deep meditative form of empathy in order to achieve it.
Probably not. Maybe.
Find a middle ground solution that nobody's happy with.
Nah.
Hmm. No.
No compromise. You'll have to deal with this head on. Somehow.
Mm.
Good. You're in control.
Take a deep breath and tell this kid to return the papers and-
You're NOT allowed!
Oh. Oh no... the anger...
The blonde kid stumbles back.
It's taking over...
Stop it! NO BURNING!
What...! But this is...
He fights you.
We're protecting Urthfolk from this filth!
Filth? How would you know, Rollo? Can you even read?
Haha, yeah! the halfling agrees.
Hey, shut it!
Guys... the dwarf girl mutters and glances at you.
She knows you're about to blow up.
Stay quiet. I'm trying to stay in control.
Typical. Reverting to dumb insults.
Urth-Nisse. Do it.
They're not listening.
I'm... I'm trying, he says, and keeps shooting sparks at the damp paper pile.
Ugh, just stop! It has to be illegal to set a fire in the middle of the street, right?
Right, Mr. Cleric?
Of course it is!
Anger brewing.
Seriously. Stop this. I'm-
Uh. No it's not.
The silent kid in the back keeps nodding profusely.
Burn it! Come on!
The rage enters your heart.
"THAT'S IT."
Your outburst actually makes them go silent.
I'm DONE.
They glance at each other.
Guess that works. Now, Cleric, what if-
Someone has to die for this!
...Excuse me?
Die?
Execution. Right now. One of you.
There's a stunned silence sweeping over the previously rowdy street.
And since you all love democracy so damn much... (Take a step forward.)
...What's he doing?
Each of you vote. You got ten seconds. Person with the most votes gets the honors. (Stand in between them and point to a spot where the execution will take place.)
You can't... do that?
W-wait a second...
<shake>NOW!</shake>
The large kid lifts his hand and points towards Rollo.
Don't vote for me, you asshole!
What the fuck...?
Rollo. Should we, uh... get the hells outta here?
Your companion stays silent.
A smirk?
He is trying really hard not to laugh his ass off.
The blonde kid quickly grabs the stack of papers and tosses it to the girls.
Fuck this. RUN!
The second Modissa grabs the stack she mutters something under her breath - then she and her girlfriends all rush away as well.
Within seconds, the two sides disperse.
The goblin gives you a shrug. "Unorthodox. A bit crazy. But hey, it worked."
(Take a deep breath, and let the rage dissipate.)
A true display of power.
Uh. You weren't actually going to...
He slides a finger across his neck.
Sure did.
Okay. Cool. Sure.
I... really believe you.
E-(Leave. Now.)
An argument...
Both sides here are legally in the wrong. So if you wish for her to give up her claims and leave, you need to find another angle.
Hmm...
An angle that you have not considered yet. One that is not obvious.
Threaten physical violence?
Maybe I could pay them off?
Wait, who's actually in charge here?
No.
No. They care not for wealth.
Ah. Yes.
Her boss. The one who does not have the license.
This kind of copper press organization is not necessarily illegal under city code.
But it is in a gray zone. And there are many forces who wish to shut them down for good.
What if you...
You. Girl with the glasses.
She meets your gaze with a frown.
You have a chance to walk away now. Before I'm forced to take this up the chain.
Everything will be shut down if you don't let this go.
Her eyes widen.
Breathing intensifies.
She's entering fight or flight.
A scoff. "So what, you'll just... what?"
I'd gladly slam the hammer on this whole thing, if you give me the chance.
I don't want to. Don't force me.
(Just nod slowly.)
She laughs.
The dwarf and halfling behind her are very quiet as she stops laughing.
Her eyes show fear.
Okay. Sure. Fine.
She throws her arms up into the air. "Fuck it."
Puff out your chest.
Take a deep breath.
(Place a hand on his shoulder.)
Your gloved hand grabs him firmly and he gives you a freaked out expression.
Kid. Give her back the papers.
Uh, he mutters, trying to form an argument.
No. Stay quiet.
He glares at you.
Give. Back. The papers.
He glances away from you.
You can see his mind working behind those wide eyes.
Then he slowly nods.
It is time.
For a compromise.
Both of you. Listen up.
Your calm and determined voice rings out across the street.
Tell the girls, "You can't deliver your paper." Then tell the boys, "And you can't steal it."
You. Can't. Deliver it.
That's what I've been saying! They've-
And you. Can't. Take it.
Just listen to him. Come on.
The blonde kid grits his teeth. Then he grabs the stack of papers and tosses it across.
Ouf...! Modissa grunts as she catches it.
Then she immediately turns to you. "What do you mean? We have every right to-"
No. Delivering. Without. A license.
Fine.
The boys quickly disperse, muttering among themselves.
Don't, the dwarf girl tells Modissa, as she strolls up to you.
Hey, Mr. Cleric? You know we're just going to deliver these anyway, right?
I'm counting on it. (Give her a thumbs up.)
Just do it a bit later. So that blonde kid doesn't notice.
I don't care. Just stop causing trouble.
If I catch you doing that, you're heading to the stockade.
As you answer, she turns and walks away.
Well. You sure made the problem go away. Somewhat.
Now let's get out of here.
Go.
The air glimmers.
What are you...!
Woah...
You encompass the two arguing kids in your Zone.
This is an official city interrogation. Answer my questions. Silence is illegal.
Please answer my questions.
Is this divine magic? I think it's very cool, he says, and frowns.
Wait... why am I...? Now I am also a little scared.
You can't just- I don't like it when you cast magic on me.
I feel violated. What? Why am I...?
Interrogation magic? I feel compelled to speak the truth.
The two of them look incredibly uncomfortable.
The spell is working. Now ask away.
Why are you so angry?
Are you doing anything illegal here?
What color is the sky?
Who is to blame here?
Are any of you guys evil?
I'm hungry, any of you hungry?
Because I feel powerless and alienated from society.
She clutches her mouth.
Because those like me used to be in charge, and now those not like me are in charge.
He goes, "Huh..." and looks down.
Yes.
Yeah.
They both look at each other, then at you.
Blue?
Yeah, blue!
She is.
He is.
Bad question. Too subjective.
No!
No.
Wait... are you saying that because you believe it, or because it's objectively true?
Uh. I don't know?
Yeah. What she said.
Fucking hells.
All the teenagers shake their heads.
Are you fucking with us?
The magic fades and the two of them look relieved.
You hear her whisper something to her friends.
She whispered, 'I hate clerics.'
That was... intense.
Come on. Let's make something happen here.
Uh.
You see the silent kid in the back take a few steps away.
She nods slowly. "Maybe... we could make a..."
As you say, compromise.
It pains her to say the word.
You see the magic enforce a sudden friendly demeanor.
Mr. Cleric. What do you think we should do?
Modissa?
I think you should leave.
She nods. "Fine. Okay."
What? But...
Let's go. It's for the best.
Oh. Uh... hey, I- what do you think we should do?
Rollo?
